title: Rock formations: the empty 12-60 cell band, filled
question: One of these has the new residual pass. Do the tall spires read to you as rock that survived while the land around it wore away — or as slabs pasted onto the skyline? And is the SIZE right now, independent of the shape?
context_md:
Canyon seed 7, same world, four-shot traverse across 2048 columns. This is the band you named when you said rock formations are 5/10/20/40 ft: the player is 14 cells, so your range is 12–120 cells, and that band was **completely empty** before — the tallest thing in the whole world at reach 15 was 4–10 cells.

**Measured, same seed:**

| prominence | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| reach 15 max | 8–10 | **25–73** |
| reach 15 p99 | ~4 | **18–26** |
| reach 30 max | 8–10 | **69–71** |

The agent also proved the diagnosis before building: it instrumented erosion's loop and found max prominence **monotonically decreasing from iteration 0**, with **0 of 2048 columns** ever peaking above 15 and later falling. So erosion never creates a residual to protect — no rate retune could have produced one, and it had to be constructed directly. That is a real finding and it closes a question I had left open.

**My own read, which I would rather you overrule than agree with politely:** the scale is right and the shape is not. To me they read as flat vertical slabs — straight sides, uniform width, flat top — rising abruptly from flat ground with no talus at the foot and no broken profile. The pair at the far left looks like two fence posts. It is the *same* failure as the cave formations you called 'all 1 pixel thick': the shape is authored as extents rather than as a profile, so it comes out a rectangle at every scale.

**Also in:** boulders re-derived to the real 3x structural rule — visible height p50 **16**, max **30** over 600 seeds, against 1–2 cells before.
